newsitem.title: GERMANY: German forwarders criticise short-notice end to surcharge.
newsitem.headline: German forwarders criticise short-notice end to surcharge.

text.p: The German freight forwarders association BSL said it welcomed the decision of Lufthansa Cargo to drop its fuel surcharge.
But it criticised the extreme short-notice of the announcement on April 10 to end the 10 U.S. cents per kg surcharge on April 15.

BSL airfreight expert Reinhard Lankes said in a statement provided to Reuters: "For freight agents the high administration costs and the constant justification of this surcharge to shippers has finally fallen.
"The additional costs for agents have not been honoured by the carriers with a single pfennig," he added.
Forwarders had reacted to the short-term dropping of the surcharge with "a lack of understanding" and had not been officially informed two working days before its end, Lankes said.
"The oft-stated partnership relationship of Lufthansa Cargo to agents still appears to be in need of improvement," he added.
The BSL now expected other airlines in Germany to follow the Lufthansa Cargo move. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax+5017
